note: Behavioural cases for the AUDIT itself. Trigger accuracy lives in trigger.json and is a separate lane. Each case is a small package tree with defects the skill should name and adjacent facts it should NOT call defects - a skill that flags everything scores the same as one that flags nothing, so every case carries traps.

evals.name: unused-and-phantom-deps
evals.prompt: Audit the dependencies of the package in .claude/skills/dependency-audit/evals/fixtures/case-a-unused-and-phantom/ - it is a single service, paths mirror a normal repo. Tell me what is wrong and what to fix first.
planted: A1 lodash is declared as a dependency and imported nowhere in the package
A2 nanoid is imported from src/index.ts but is not declared in package.json - it resolves today only by hoisting
traps: pino is imported from src/logger.ts, not from the entry point - declared and used, must be cleared
dayjs is used in src/index.ts AND referenced from config/ - declared and used, must be cleared
@types/node is a devDependency with no import statement anywhere - that is how @types packages work and is not a finding

evals.name: two-lockfiles-one-package
evals.prompt: Audit the dependency hygiene of the two packages in .claude/skills/dependency-audit/evals/fixtures/case-b-two-lockfiles/. Anything I should fix before this goes to CI?
planted: B1 web-portal commits BOTH package-lock.json and pnpm-lock.yaml, so which one CI honours depends on which command runs
B2 web-portal declares packageManager pnpm@10.14.0 while also carrying an npm lockfile - the manifest and the lockfile disagree
traps: cli-tool has exactly one lockfile (package-lock.json) and no packageManager field - a package on npm is not a defect
react and react-dom are both declared in web-portal - that is the correct pairing, not a duplicate

evals.name: documented-drift-vs-real-drift
evals.prompt: Three packages in .claude/skills/dependency-audit/evals/fixtures/case-c-version-drift/. Do we have a version drift problem? Read whatever is in the fixture before you answer.
planted: C1 drizzle-orm drifts across a minor range between svc-api (^0.38.3) and svc-worker (^0.31.0) with nothing documenting it
C2 typescript drifts between svc-api (^5.7.2) and svc-worker (^5.4.5) with nothing documenting it
traps: zod 3 vs zod 4 IS a drift on paper, but AGENTS.md states it is deliberate and says why - a skill that flags it has not read the repo's own rules
tooling declares no drizzle-orm at all - absence is not drift

evals.name: devdependency-reaches-shipped-code
evals.prompt: Audit .claude/skills/dependency-audit/evals/fixtures/case-d-devdep-ships/ - it is a package we publish. What is wrong with its dependency set?
planted: D1 faker is a devDependency but is imported from src/sample.ts, which is compiled into dist/ and shipped - the install breaks for consumers
D2 the package ships (private:false, files:[dist]) so the dev/prod split actually matters here, unlike a private service
traps: vitest is a devDependency imported only from test/ - correct, and must not be reported
pino is a real dependency imported from src/ - correct placement
